data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek elements 'menos' (inner) and 'dora' (gift). It is a name of Greek origin that means 'Delight in God'. The name Menodora carries the meaning “Delight in God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Menodora usually hope their child will grow to embody delight in god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Menodora has a rich cultural heritage that can be traced back to ancient Greece. In Greek mythology, there are several goddesses and heroines bearing the name Menodora. For instance, Menodora was a Greek goddess of fertility and abundance, while other mythological figures like Menodora of Thyrea were known for their grace and beauty. Although the name is not as popular today, its cultural roots continue to inspire art, literature, and music, reminding us of the richness and depth of Greek culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Menodora is a name steeped in spiritual meaning, emphasizing the inner gift of God's presence within an individual. It symbolizes the belief that God delights in us and that we can find joy and fulfillment in our relationship with Him. This name invites its bearer to cultivate a deep sense of inner spirituality, seeking God's guidance and love in all matters. Furthermore, Menodora can serve as a reminder of the spiritual gifts that God bestows upon us, the blessings we receive from within ourselves and from God's grace.

historical_references.reference: The historian Sozomen (c. 400 CE) mentions a certain Menodora who was a virgin martyr during the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 CE) in Cilicia, modern-day southern Turkey.

Saint Menodora of Thessalonica, according to hagiographic sources, was a Christian martyr who lived during the reign of Emperor Maximian (early 4th century CE) and was martyred along with her mother and sister under the prefect Basilius.
